title: Store water
summary: How much to keep, what to keep it in, and when to swap it out.

cards.headline: Store one gallon per person per day
cards.body: Keep at least a 3-day supply ready to grab, and aim for 2 weeks at home. That covers drinking plus basic cooking and cleaning.

cards.headline: Some people need more than a gallon
cards.body: Children, nursing mothers, and people who are sick need more. Very hot weather can double how much anyone needs, so store extra if you live somewhere hot.

cards.headline: Sealed store-bought water is the easiest supply
cards.body: Commercially bottled water is the safest choice. Keep it sealed in its original container until you need it, and watch the use-by date.

cards.headline: Any old plastic jug works for storing water
cards.body: Use food-grade water containers or clean 2-liter soda bottles. Skip milk and juice jugs, because leftover protein and sugar grow bacteria. Skip glass, which is heavy and breaks.

cards.headline: Wash and sanitize bottles before filling them
cards.body: Wash with dish soap and rinse well. Swish a mix of 1 teaspoon unscented bleach per quart of water over every surface, then rinse it out with clean water.

cards.headline: Fill to the top with tap water
cards.body: City tap water treated with chlorine needs nothing added. Well water or untreated water gets 2 drops of unscented bleach per 2-liter bottle. Cap it without touching the inside of the cap.

cards.headline: Date it, store it dark, swap it every 6 months
cards.body: Write the fill date on each bottle. Keep them somewhere cool and dark. Replace home-filled water every 6 months. Store-bought water follows its use-by date.
